column1: # Declared nondeterminism in the pinned tour executable denominator.
# Sprint 118 / Story #4 / Story-ID 759341a95870.
# STATUS: MEASUREMENT RECORD. This table records WHAT was measured to be
# nondeterministic and why. It grants nothing by itself: an annotation carried
# on an observation is diagnosis, and tools/tour/executor-selftests.rb asserts
# that a ledger claiming this table has waiver effect is rejected by name
# (`volatility:claims_gate_effect`).
# The adjudication that followed lives in docs/tour/semantics.tsv, which binds
# each of these eleven rows to a reviewed comparator in tools/tour/semantics.rb.
# The two tables must name EXACTLY the same rows: tools/tour/executor-runner.rb
# and tools/tour/executor-gate.rb both reject a comparator for a row nobody
# measured, and a measured volatile row left without one. The comparators are
# anchored to repeated observations of the CURRENT native binary, not to the
# historical draw recorded in tests/tour/results.tsv.
# Why it exists: tour-executor/v1 reproduces the accepted observations in
# tests/tour/results.tsv for 83 of the 93 applicable rows and for all 4
# build-only rows, and fails on the rows below. Those are not
# regressions and not a harness defect: their output depends on the wall clock,
# the randomly seeded global PRNG, goroutine interleaving or Go's randomized
# map iteration order, so no byte-exact accepted digest can be reproducible for
# them. The pinned accepted baseline captured one instance of each.
# RESOLUTION (sprint-118 plan §6, second option): explicit reviewed semantic
# comparators — see docs/tour/semantics.tsv. Masking them in
# tools/tour/normalize.rb was and remains rejected: the normalizer's v1 rules
# stay minimal, and a mask wide enough to hide a timestamp or a PRNG draw would
# also hide a real numeric or causal error. The comparators do the opposite of
# masking — they check the value's support, the event multiplicities, the causal
# order and the timing conditions, and they compare exit status and stderr
# byte-exactly.
# The set was MEASURED, not guessed, in two passes.
#   Pass 1 — all 93 applicable rows were built with the pinned Go 1.27.0
#   toolchain and executed SEVEN times each under LC_ALL=C. Seven rows produced
#   more than one distinct output: basics/packages.go (6 distinct),
#   concurrency/default-selection.go (7), concurrency/goroutines.go (5),
#   methods/errors.go (7), solutions/stringers.go (2),
#   solutions/webcrawler.go (7), welcome/sandbox.go (7).
#   Pass 2 — the remaining rows whose fresh baseline did not reproduce the
#   pinned accepted digest. These are stable within one burst but not across
#   calendar time or process instances: flowcontrol/switch-evaluation-order.go
#   and flowcontrol/switch-with-no-condition.go branch on the current
#   weekday/hour, and methods/exercise-stringer.go ranges over a two-entry map
#   whose iteration order Go randomizes per process.
#   Pass 3 — Sprint 118 story 4 re-review of concurrency/channels.go
#   (759341a95870). Pass 1 had classified it byte-identical because one
#   seven-run burst drew one order; that classification was WRONG. The program
#   launches two INDEPENDENT sums on one unbuffered channel and receives two
#   values in arrival order: the synchronization guarantees both values and
#   the printed sum, but nothing orders which sender wins. A bounded
#   experiment on the native binary freshly built from the byte-identical
#   source with the pinned go1.27.0 (LC_ALL=C, empty PATH, fresh cwd per run;
#   raw commands/status/streams retained under
#   /Users/qiangli/.local/state/bashy/sprint118-evidence/tour-channel-order-review)
#   witnessed BOTH legal orders under GOMAXPROCS 1/2/4: "-5 17 12" in
#   1204/1207 runs, "17 -5 12" in 3/1207 (GOMAXPROCS=2: 1/400; GOMAXPROCS=4:
#   2/400; GOMAXPROCS=1: 0/400), every run exit 0 with stdout exactly 9 bytes
#   and empty stderr. A seven-run GOMAXPROCS=2 burst — the oracle shape —
#   still drew one single order 7/7, which is exactly why pass 1 measured it
#   as stable. The support is exactly two whole outputs.
# Rows deliberately NOT listed: concurrency/mutex-counter.go,
# concurrency/range-and-close.go, concurrency/select.go,
# solutions/binarytrees.go and solutions/binarytrees_quit.go all use
# goroutines but were byte-identical across seven runs — they synchronize, so
# they stay under exact comparison.
# `comparator_needed` names the control or comparator the row requires. Each is
# now IMPLEMENTED and bound in docs/tour/semantics.tsv; this column stays as the
# statement of what the measurement asked for, so the implementation can be read
# against the requirement.
